Beige Book cross-check (May 2017) supports the FOMC’s cautiously positive stance: most Districts reported modest-to-moderate growth; labor markets tightened further with wage gains concentrated among skilled workers; energy sector activity improved; tourism provided a tailwind in several areas. Housing remained comparatively firmer than commercial real estate, where conditions were softer. Lending volumes were generally steady, but credit standards tightened for CRE and were firmer for autos, aligning with a mixed but not broadly restrictive credit backdrop. Inflation pressures remained modest.

Net: The Beige Book corroborates continued moderate expansion and further labor tightening, while acknowledging below-target inflation and sector-specific frictions (CRE, autos). Relative to a SLOOS-only read, the broader base of growth and labor strength warrants a small upward adjustment in tone.
